s: A weathered old man in a grey cross-collared hanfu and cloth headwrap leans on a wooden staff at the gate of a frontier beacon tower, one hand shading his eyes as a horse disappears down a dusty road; three worried neighbours in muted brown robes cluster behind him, one wringing his hands, another gesturing toward the empty road. Dry grass, packed-earth wall, layered blue mountains at dusk, calm and unhurried mood.

A palace courtyard with red lacquered pillars and grey tiled eaves; a row of children in bright cross-collared hanfu proudly holds pots of blooming flowers, while a small boy in a patched pale-blue robe hugs an empty clay pot, eyes downcast, cheeks flushed with shame; an old king in dark gold-trimmed robes kneels down to smile at him, one hand on the boy's shoulder.

Beside a clear mountain stream, an old woman in a faded blue headscarf and patched hemp robe sits on a flat rock, sleeves tied back, patiently rubbing a thick iron rod against a wet grey whetstone, her lined face serene; a boy in a scholar's pale robe with hair in two buns leans in wide-eyed, hands on his knees, mouth open in surprise. Willow branches, mossy stones, sparkling water.

A tearful woodcutter boy in a coarse brown short jacket and straw sandals kneels at a misty lakeshore, wiping his eyes with his sleeve, an empty rope belt hanging where his old axe was; a white-bearded immortal in flowing silver-white robes rises from the water holding up a shining gold axe in one hand and a silver axe in the other, kind eyes crinkled, water sliding off his sleeves.

A dark wooden palace hall lit by bronze lamps; a short, composed envoy in a deep-blue robe and black gauze cap holds up a plump orange in one hand and a knobbly bitter fruit in the other, eyebrows raised in calm confidence; around him armoured Chu officials in red and black lean forward with sceptical smirks, one whispering behind his sleeve, while the king on the dais narrows his eyes.

Snow-covered northern grassland under a pale grey sky; a gaunt man in a worn sheepskin coat over a faded red hanfu stands straight against the wind, clutching a tasselled bamboo envoy staff to his chest, beard frosted white, jaw set and eyes steady; a small flock of sheep huddles behind a low rock, breath steaming in the cold air.

In a bustling Han-era market street, a sturdy man in a dark green robe with rolled sleeves clasps forearms with a merchant in a blue apron, both laughing openly, a small crowd of townsfolk nodding and smiling around them; stalls of cloth, grain sacks and hanging bronze scales, wooden shop fronts with plain blank signboards, warm afternoon light and drifting dust.

An artist in a loose ink-grey robe and topknot kneels on a low stool before a white plastered wall, brush lifted mid-stroke, eyes bright with mischief; four black ink dragons coil across the wall without pupils, while two finished dragons peel away from the plaster into swirls of cloud, pupils glinting, mouths open, trailing ink droplets. A stunned crowd in simple robes clutches at their hats in the doorway.

In a bronze-and-red throne hall, a young king in a black robe with gold dragon patterns leans forward on his seat, one hand gripping the armrest, eyes suddenly sharp and commanding; a kneeling minister in grey holds up a small wooden bird carving, eyebrows raised in question. Behind the throne a painted screen shows a huge bird with wings spread wide, about to launch into the sky.

A calm painter in a grey scholar robe sits cross-legged in a bamboo-framed studio, brush poised above a still-blank silk scroll, eyes closed and a small confident smile on his lips; through the round lattice window a bamboo grove sways, its shadow falling faintly across the empty paper. Inkstone, brush rack, a cup of tea, soft green light.

A farmhouse courtyard kitchen: a guest in a blue robe points urgently at a straight brick chimney standing beside a tall stack of dry firewood, eyebrows up, mouth open in warning; the host in a brown apron waves a hand dismissively, half turned away, still holding a teapot. Clay jars, wooden buckets, a low stove, warm late afternoon sunlight and floating dust.

Inside a command tent, a strategist in a dark blue robe and leather cap leans over a sand table map, one finger pressed on a small walled-city marker, expression keen and certain; two armoured generals in lamellar armour lean in, one stroking his beard as understanding dawns, the other frowning at the alternate route marked by wooden pegs. Bronze lamps, plain banners, tent poles.

In a sunlit village square, four blind men in simple grey and brown hanfu, each wearing a cloth blindfold, gather around a gentle grey elephant and touch different parts: one hugs a leg, one flaps a big ear, one holds the trunk, one pats the flank. Their faces show puzzlement and argument, mouths open, free hands gesturing at one another, while the elephant stands patiently with a mild eye.

A night army camp: a general in partial lamellar armour sits on a wooden crate beside a small fire, a bamboo scroll unrolled on his knee, one hand still resting on his sword hilt; his helmet lies on the ground beside him, brows drawn in concentration, lips slightly moving as he reads. Tents and stacked spears behind, sparks rising, warm firelight on his face.

A bare mud-brick room at night; a thin boy in a patched hemp robe kneels on the floor, a bamboo scroll open on a low wooden board, his face lit by a single warm beam of light coming through a small chiselled hole in the wall; his eyes are wide and eager, one hand raised to shield the glare, the rest of the room in soft blue shadow.

A Han-dynasty reception room: a nervous guest in a green robe recoils from a wine cup on a low table, both hands raised, eyes wide at the curved shadow inside the cup; his host in grey points calmly at a large decorated bow hanging on the wall behind, candlelight stretching the bow's reflection across the cup. Lacquered dishes, a bronze censer, warm lamp glow.

A riverbank at dawn: a commanding general in dark red armour with a billowing cape stands on a rock, arm raised in a decisive gesture; soldiers in lamellar armour smash bronze cauldrons with wooden mallets, while others watch the last boat gurgle beneath the water. Dust, spray, torn banners, determined faces lit by low golden sun.

An elderly couple in worn travelling robes stand in a blossoming courtyard, each holding half of a broken bronze mirror; they fit the halves together between them, the crack glowing faintly, both laughing with tears in their eyes, grey hair in simple buns, sleeves touching. Fallen petals, a low stone wall, soft spring light, tender reunion mood.

A market stall under a cloth awning: a stunned merchant in a blue robe stares at a gleaming white pearl left alone on the counter, palms turned up in disbelief; walking away is a delighted customer in a yellow robe cradling a carved, gem-inlaid wooden box, chin high, eyes shining. Bolts of silk, a spice jar, a curious onlooker scratching his head.

A crowded market lane at closing time; a flustered man in a brown robe stands at a shoe stall holding up a knotted straw measuring cord, gesturing helplessly at his own bare feet, mouth open in dismay; the shoe seller in an apron shrugs with crossed arms. Other vendors roll up mats behind them, an empty street beyond, comic frustration.

A grand Qin court hall with black and red lacquered pillars; a powerful minister in a long black robe holds a lead rope attached to a calm spotted deer with small antlers, chin lifted, eyes challenging; rows of officials in tall caps hesitate, some lowering their heads, one old minister frowning with pressed lips and clenched fists inside his sleeves.

A riverbank with a wooden boat moored close to shore; a small boy in a light blue robe crouches at the boat rail, carving a mark on the hull at the waterline with a knife, tongue between his teeth in concentration; a huge grey elephant waits on the bank with its keeper, and officials in tall caps watch with folded arms, one leaning over the water to see the mark.

A courtyard gate at dusk; a sneaky man in a dark short jacket tiptoes on a wooden stool, both hands clamped over his own ears, eyes squeezed shut, one arm stretching toward a bronze door bell hanging from the gate beam; a cat on the wall watches him with flat unimpressed eyes. Moon rising, long shadows, comic tension.

A palace side hall; an earnest minister in a grey robe kneels and carefully places one more egg on top of a tall, wobbling stack of eggs on a lacquered tray, holding his breath, brows knitted; the king in a red and gold robe leans out from his seat, eyebrows high, both hands braced on the armrests. Tension, soft indoor light, single point of balance.

A village lane beside a stream; a plain-featured woman in a garish pink robe and crooked hairpin walks with an exaggerated frown and a hand pressed to her chest, chin jutting; three villagers hurry the other way, one hiding a smile behind a sleeve, a child peeking out from behind a laundry basket. Willow tree, ducks on the water, gentle comic tone.

A misty Guizhou mountain path with tall grass; a small grey donkey stands braced on stiff legs, mouth wide open mid-bray, one hind hoof lifted; a golden-orange tiger peeks out from behind a thick tree trunk, ears flat, eyes wide with startled curiosity, hind legs ready to bolt. Dappled green light, ferns, a winding trail.

Under a willow by a stone table, a smug painter in a green robe kneels and adds four little legs to a completed ink snake on a paper scroll, brush tip delicate, tongue at the corner of his mouth; beside him a second man in brown springs up holding a wine pot aloft, laughing and pointing at the extra feet. Ink stone, spilled wine, scattered brushes.

A hillside at night after a retreat; exhausted soldiers in dusty armour crouch behind rocks, one pointing with a shaking hand at wind-shaken bushes that look like crouching figures in the moonlight; fear on their faces, eyes wide, breath fogging. Broken banners, abandoned spears, low mist between the trees.

An archery range at golden hour; a lean archer in a fitted blue training robe with a leather arm guard draws a bow, the string against his cheek, one eye narrowed in total focus; a row of straw targets behind him bristles with arrows clustered dead centre. A crowd of onlookers murmurs behind a rope, one child on tiptoe.

A village lane before a thatched gate; a young scholar in a wrinkled blue robe scratches his head with an awkward, embarrassed grin, one hand raised as if reciting a line; an eager neighbour in a straw hat leans in, hands on knees, mouth open in hope. A blank notice board stands in the far background, chickens pecking, soft afternoon light.

A poor cottage at night; a boy in a patched grey robe sits at a rough wooden desk holding up a small white gauze bag full of glowing fireflies, his face lit by pale green-gold light, eyes wide with delight; through the open window behind him moonlit snow glows blue-white. Scrolls, an ink slab, a thin blanket.

A hillside command post framed by pines; a young strategist in a white robe and black headwrap holds a feather fan across his chest, pointing calmly down into a valley where tiny armoured soldiers move in formation; two generals in armour stand behind him, mouths open in admiration. Morning mist, fluttering banners, layered mountains.

At the foot of two enormous green mountains, a white-bearded old man in a short work jacket and straw sandals carries a bamboo basket of earth on a shoulder pole, back bent but eyes bright and determined; behind him sons and grandsons dig with hoes and a small boy carries a tiny basket. A smirking neighbour watches from a rock, arms folded.

A forest path; a smug little orange fox struts ahead with tail high and chin lifted, glancing back over its shoulder with a sly grin; a huge tiger pads behind it, brow furrowed in confusion; rabbits, deer and monkeys scatter into the bushes on both sides, eyes wide. Sunbeams through leaves, ferns, fallen logs.

A wooden dining table: a thin man in a grey robe pushes a bowl of rice away with both hands, leaning back, face pale, lips pressed and eyes wary; a friend in brown leans across the table, chopsticks raised mid-argument, expression exasperated but kind. Steam curling from a soup bowl, a teapot, two empty cups.

A cottage interior with a wooden loom; a woman in a blue cotton robe and headscarf holds large shears, having just cut the half-woven cloth, loose threads hanging, her expression firm and sad; in the doorway a travel-dusted young man in a scholar robe drops his bundle, head lowered in shame. Sunlight through paper window, dust motes.

Close framing: an old woman's weathered hands, sleeves rolled, grind a thick iron rod against a wet grey stone, water droplets and iron filings glinting; her lined face is serene with a small smile; a boy's round face peeks in from the left edge, eyes huge with wonder. Stream, bamboo leaves, soft green light.

A riverside pavilion among pines; a musician in a pale grey robe sits before a seven-stringed qin on a stone table, fingers plucking, eyes half closed, expression transported; across from him a woodcutter in a plain brown robe sits on a rock listening with his whole face, one hand lifted as if following the melody. Waterfall, mist, drifting leaves.

A family hall with a low wooden table; four children in bright hanfu cluster around a plate of yellow pears; the smallest boy, hair in two buns, holds a tiny pear with both hands and a pleased smile, while older boys hold large pears and grin; the father in a dark robe watches with a hand on his beard, delighted. Warm lamplight, wooden pillars.

A market street; a foolish scholar in a wrinkled robe holds a green leaf over one eye and reaches with the other hand for a bolt of cloth on a stall, tongue out in concentration, convinced he is invisible; the stallholder grabs his wrist, eyebrows raised, and bystanders turn with amused faces. Hanging cloth, baskets of fruit, bright daylight.

A simple classroom with bamboo mats and a low desk; an old teacher in a dark grey robe with a long beard holds up one corner of a wooden square tile, eyebrows raised in a question; a young student in pale blue sits forward, hand shooting up, face bright with understanding as he sketches three more corners in the air with his finger.

A Handan street; elegant townsfolk in flowing robes walk gracefully past, chins high, sleeves swaying; in the foreground a mortified young traveller in a dusty robe crawls on hands and knees, one sandal lost, face red, looking up at the passers-by while a small dog watches curiously. Comic, gentle, warm daylight.

A court hall; a minister in a blue robe taps his lips then his teeth with two fingers, expression urgent, eyebrows drawn together; on a lacquered table before the seated king lie a jade disc and a small bronze horse figurine. The king in red and gold rests his chin on one hand, unimpressed, while a chancellor behind him frowns.

A richly decorated study full of dragon motifs: carved dragon pillars, dragon-patterned screens, a dragon-embroidered robe on a stand; a nobleman in green and gold robes scrambles backwards over a fallen stool, face pale, mouth open in a scream; a real blue-green dragon's enormous head fills the round window, one gentle eye blinking, whiskers curling in the breeze.

Low viewpoint on a dirt road: a small green mantis stands on tiptoe in the middle of the track, forelegs raised high in a defiant pose, tiny face fierce; a huge wooden chariot wheel with bronze spokes looms over it, dust swirling, horse legs blurred with motion behind. Dramatic scale contrast, warm dusty light.

On a wooden riverboat mid-stream; a calm man in a blue robe kneels at the gunwale, knife in hand, carefully carving a notch beside a coil of rope; behind him the water ripples where a sword just sank, a few bubbles rising. The boatman in a straw cape looks back over his shoulder with a puzzled frown. River hills, soft daylight.

A narrow lane: a resolute mother in a plain blue robe and cloth headscarf carries a cloth bundle on her back and holds a small boy's hand, walking toward a schoolhouse with a tiled roof where child silhouettes recite at the window; behind them a market stall and a graveyard slope are visible. She looks determined, the boy curious and wide-eyed.

A hillside sheep pen in the morning; a shepherd in a brown jacket kneels hammering a wooden plank over a broken gap in the fence, sleeves rolled up, jaw set with resolve; sheep crowd safely inside, bleating; wolf paw prints dot the mud outside, and one sheep looks at him with a grateful tilt of its head.

The courtyard gate of a grand house; a burly general, armour removed, bare back criss-crossed by a bundle of thorn branches tied on, kneels with head bowed, jaw tight and eyes wet; a slim minister in a white robe hurries down the steps, both hands outstretched to raise him, expression warm and forgiving. Stone lions, tiled eaves, morning light.

A frontier stable yard at dusk: an old man in a grey robe and fur-trimmed hat strokes the neck of a newly arrived wild horse among several others, calm half-smile on his weathered face; neighbours crowd at the gate with congratulatory gestures, one holding up a wine jar; a doubtful neighbour in the back scratches his chin. Warm orange light, wooden fences.

A city gate tower with a plain wooden frame; a thick bundle of bamboo scrolls hangs from the gate, and beneath it a small chest overflowing with gold pieces sits on a table; curious townsfolk in varied robes crowd around, one scholar leaning close to the scrolls and scratching his chin, others whispering, a guard watching with folded arms.

A carpenter's workshop; a craftsman in a sleeveless work vest peels a thin shaving from a wooden board with a plane, revealing black ink brush strokes sunk deep into the grain; his eyes are wide with astonishment, mouth open; beside him a scholar in a grey robe leans in, equally amazed. Wood shavings curl on the floor, sawdust in the light.

A grassy riverbank; a musician in a light grey robe sits on a flat rock with a qin across his knees, playing with great feeling, eyes closed, head tilted; two paces away a brown cow chews grass, one ear flicked, eyes utterly indifferent, tail swishing. Willow branches and slow water behind, comic contrast, warm afternoon.

A dim official chamber; a large bronze vat sits over glowing charcoal, heat shimmer rising; a smooth-faced official in a black robe gestures toward it with an open palm and a thin smile; opposite him a stout official in red has gone pale, sweat on his brow, hands raised in protest, mouth open. Cold blue light from a high window, hot orange from the coals.

A dusty summer road; a general in red armour on horseback points with his whip toward a distant grove, expression confident and sly; behind him exhausted soldiers in light armour trudge with cracked lips, but several have straightened up, eyes brightening, one licking his lips. Heat haze, wilted grass, cicada-filled air, strong sunlight.

A market courtyard; an old oil seller in a patched apron holds a long-handled ladle high and pours a thin steady stream of golden oil through the square hole of a bronze coin balanced on a gourd's mouth; his face is calm, eyes focused; a proud archer in a blue robe watches, eyebrows climbing in disbelief, hands on hips.

A palace music hall; a long row of musicians in matching blue robes play the yu, cheeks puffed; one man in the middle holds his instrument slightly wrong and puffs his cheeks theatrically with eyes darting sideways to copy his neighbours; the seated king in gold taps his foot, unaware. Lacquered screens, bronze bells, warm lamp light.

A green rice field; a farmer in a straw hat and rolled-up trousers kneels between rows, pulling a young seedling upward with both hands, face gleaming with sweat and self-satisfaction; behind him rows of seedlings stand unnaturally tall and tilted, soil disturbed. A boy at the field edge stares with open mouth, a buffalo swishing its tail nearby.

A council hall with bronze candle stands; a plain-robed retainer in brown steps out from a row of seated guests, one hand on his chest, chin high, eyes determined; he holds up a cloth bag with the sharp tip of an awl poking through the fabric; the nobleman in a purple robe turns with a sceptical raised eyebrow, fingers drumming the table.

A Qin palace hall; a resolute envoy in a blue robe stands with his back almost against a carved pillar, holding a round white jade disc high above his head with both hands, eyes blazing, jaw set; the king in black and gold half rises from his throne, one hand outstretched, face alarmed; courtiers freeze mid-gesture. Dramatic side light.

A bright child's room in an old Chinese house; a small girl in a pink cross-collared robe sits at a low desk with an open picture scroll, fingertip tracing an unnoticed corner detail, mouth forming a round O of surprise, eyes sparkling; a stack of already-read scrolls tied with ribbon beside her. Paper window, warm sunlight, wooden floor.

A village schoolroom; a teacher in a dark robe holds up a wooden tally stick and points at a simple chart of jobs, expression clear and firm; four children in blue and green robes stand in a neat line, each holding a small tool, a broom, a watering can and an inkstone, nodding earnestly. Lattice window, bamboo desks.

A courtyard at cold blue dawn; a rooster on the fence crows with its neck stretched; two young men in white training robes practise swords on the stone paving, one mid-swing with sleeves flying, faces flushed and determined, breath visible in the cold air; a lantern still burning low by the door, frost on the tiles.

A busy market stall hung with spears and round shields; a boastful vendor in a red vest holds up a shield in one hand and a spear in the other, chest puffed, mouth open mid-boast; a bystander in a grey robe raises one finger with a sly questioning smile, and the crowd leans in grinning. Dust, awning, stacked goods.

In front of a fine wooden gate with carved eaves; a cocky young man in a short jacket swings a large axe in a flashy arc, eyes on the onlookers; an older master carpenter in an ink-blue apron leans against the gatepost, arms folded, one eyebrow raised, a faint amused smile. Wood shavings and a planing bench nearby, warm daylight.

A shoreline at autumn flood: a river god with a human face and a water-serpent body stands on the wet sand, shoulders slumped, head bowed, eyes wide with awe; before him the sea stretches to a flat horizon, huge and pale, waves curling. His ornate water crown droops, his proud posture has collapsed, vast empty sky.

A courtyard with a huge glazed water vat; a calm boy in a blue robe swings a large rock down with both arms, face set; the vat's side cracks and water bursts out in an arc; other children in bright robes scatter, one crying, one running for the gate, a small shoe floating in the spreading puddle. Dynamic splash, bright daylight.

A Spartan chamber: a lean king in a plain dark robe sits on a bed of dry brushwood, a rope of bitter gall hanging above his head; he dips a finger, tastes it, and his face screws up in distaste while his eyes stay hard and steady; a bronze sword and a stack of bamboo scrolls on the floor. Dim austere light, single window.

A riverbank at low tide; a large clam has clamped its shell shut on a snipe's long beak; the bird strains backwards with wings flapping, eyes indignant; the clam glares from between its shells; in the background a fisherman in a straw cape quietly sets down his basket and creeps closer, grinning. Wet sand, reeds, morning haze.

A Wei-style banquet hall; a plump cheerful former ruler in a soft yellow robe sits on cushions, clapping and laughing at dancers, a wine cup in his other hand, eyes crinkled with genuine delight; opposite him a Wei official leans in with a probing smile, chin on hand; musicians, lanterns, swirling silk sleeves.

Inside a war tent at night: a battle-worn general in dark armour sits on a folding stool, head propped in one hand, eyes hollow; around him soldiers kneel with faces turned toward the tent flap, tears on their cheeks, listening; faint blue moonlight outside suggests distant singing, a single lamp gutters. Heavy, quiet sorrow.

A crossroads on a country road; a confident traveller in a fine blue robe sits in a well-stocked ox cart facing away from a blank wooden signpost, gesturing forward with his whip; a passing farmer in a straw hat points firmly in the opposite direction, eyebrows raised, mouth open in warning. Comic confidence, fields and distant hills.

A scholar's gate in heavy snow: a young man in a thin blue robe stands perfectly still on the stone step, hands folded inside his sleeves, snow piled on his shoulders, hat and eyebrows, breath steaming, expression calm and respectful; behind him the courtyard is white, his footprints slowly filling in. Grey sky, closed wooden door, warm light in a window.

A reed marsh at dusk; a bowman in a dark hunting robe stands with an unstrung bow, having just released the string, face calm and knowing; above, a wild goose with ruffled feathers twists in mid-air, wings flailing, eyes wide in panic, beginning to fall; the bowstring still vibrating. Golden reeds, pale sky, shadows.

A small tea house table; a man in a brown robe has stuffed whole red dates into his mouth, cheeks bulging comically, eyes watering, one hand at his throat; across the table two friends lean back in alarm, one reaching to pat his back, the other holding a pear mid-bite. Teacups, a dish of dates, a lazy cat on the windowsill.

Inside a command tent: a proud young general in ornate armour holds an open scroll and declaims with one finger raised, eyes fixed on the text, ignoring the map on the table; two veteran officers exchange worried glances, one pointing urgently at wooden markers showing an encirclement. The tent flap reveals distant dust and enemy banners.

A courtyard with a monkey keeper in a brown jacket holding up three chestnuts in one open palm and four in the other, bargaining expression, eyebrows raised; a circle of monkeys reacts vividly, some leaping angrily with fur bristling, some clapping happily, one scratching its head in confusion; baskets of acorns behind. Warm afternoon, comic energy.

A market street below a palace window; three townsmen stand in a row, each pointing dramatically at an empty spot in the street, mouths open in claim; in the window above, a king in a red robe leans out, brow furrowed, half-convinced, one hand gripping the sill; no tiger anywhere. Townsfolk whisper, laundry flapping, strong daylight.

A snow-covered thatched cottage behind a bamboo fence; a bearded man in a fur-trimmed cloak stands patiently at the gate with hands clasped, snow on his shoulders and hat, breath white, expression humble and hopeful; two attendants shiver behind him holding a horse; warm lamplight glows in the cottage window, smoke curling from the roof.

A stable yard with three pairs of horses held by grooms; a strategist in a blue robe points from one horse to another, counting on his fingers with a clever smile; a nobleman in fine robes listens with dawning excitement, one hand raised; the horses differ in build, from sleek to sturdy. Race flags, dirt track, low fence, bright morning.

A study at night: a young scholar in a white robe sits at a desk piled with bamboo scrolls, his long hair tied by a rope to a beam above so it pulls taut when he nods; one hand holds a small awl poised near his thigh, eyes red-rimmed but fiercely awake; a guttering oil lamp throws long shadows. Determination and exhaustion.

A field gone wild with tall weeds; a farmer in a straw hat sits on a wooden stool beside a tree stump, chin in hand, eyes fixed hopefully on the stump, a rusty hoe lying in the grass beside him; a rabbit-shaped cloud drifts above; in the distance a neighbour shakes his head and points at the overgrown rows.

A muddy mountain road: an overturned ox cart lies in a ditch ahead, one wheel still spinning, bundles scattered; a second carter in a straw cape reins in his ox sharply at the top of the slope, leaning forward with wide eyes, one hand raised to stop; his ox braces its legs. Rain-washed rocks, grey sky, wet grass.

Close-up beneath tiled eaves: a large grey stone with a deep smooth hollow worn in its centre, single water drops caught mid-fall from the roof edge, tiny splash crown; moss and a small sprout at the stone base; soft morning light, shallow depth, no people, calm and quietly powerful.

A study with shelves of bamboo scrolls; an elderly scholar in a dark grey robe and long beard holds up a bamboo scroll whose leather binding has snapped, the slips splayed, his expression absorbed rather than dismayed; three worn cords lie on the desk beside an ink slab, a lamp and a cup of tea. Warm indoor light, deep concentration.

A small courtyard at night; a thin man in a rumpled robe crouches with a blanket held over his head with both hands, peering up at the sky in terror, knees drawn up; a friend in a blue robe sits on a stool beside him, gesturing calmly at the stars and the solid ground, patient smile. Moonlight, a well, a potted plant.
